skills.title: Classifying Groups of Organisms
skills.description: Living things are sorted into groups by features, like backbones, feathers, or flowers. Can you sort organisms into the right groups using their features?

skills.title: What Is Biodiversity?
skills.description: Biodiversity is the variety of life on Earth: differences within a species, among species, and among habitats. Can you match each example to the right kind of variety?

skills.title: Variety Within a Species
skills.description: When members of a species are different from each other, the species is more likely to survive changes. Can you pick how this variety helps a species?

skills.title: Variety Keeps Communities Strong
skills.description: A community with many kinds of living things can bounce back after trouble like fire or disease. Can you pick which community would recover best?

skills.title: Living Things Depend on Each Other
skills.description: Living things team up, compete, and depend on their surroundings, and this helps keep many kinds of life going. Can you match each relationship to its example?

skills.title: Invasive Species
skills.description: Invasive species are newcomers that spread fast, crowd out local living things, and lower biodiversity. Can you pick how they cause harm?

skills.title: Climate Change and Biodiversity
skills.description: A warming climate changes habitats and can make species disappear. Can you pick how climate change reduces biodiversity and what happens next?

skills.title: Biodiversity and Farming
skills.description: Many kinds of crops, pollinators, and soil life help farms, including Indigenous farms around the world. Can you pick how variety helps growing food?

skills.title: Why Biodiversity Matters
skills.description: Biodiversity gives us food, medicine, clean air, and healthy nature, and losing it causes big problems. Can you pick the benefits and what happens when it shrinks?

skills.title: Protecting Local Biodiversity
skills.description: People see local nature issues in different ways, and a good plan protects living things. Can you pick helpful actions and the views of different people?

skills.title: Static Electricity
skills.description: Rubbing things can build up charges that attract or push away, like a balloon sticking to a wall. Can you pick what static electricity does in each example?

skills.title: Current and Static Electricity
skills.description: Current electricity flows steadily through a path, but static electricity stays in one place until it jumps. Can you tell them apart?

skills.title: Conductors and Insulators
skills.description: Metals let electric current flow through, and materials like rubber, plastic, and wood block it. Can you sort materials into conductors and insulators?

skills.title: Making Electrical Energy
skills.description: Devices like solar panels, generators, and batteries change other energy into electrical energy. Can you match each device to the energy it changes?

skills.title: Using Electrical Energy
skills.description: Electrical energy changes into light, heat, sound, and motion in things like lamps, toasters, and fans. Can you match each device to the energy it makes?

skills.title: Parts of a Circuit
skills.description: A simple circuit has a power source, wires, a switch, and a load like a bulb. Can you label each part and pick its job?

skills.title: Series and Parallel Circuits
skills.description: In a series circuit there is one path, and in a parallel circuit there are many paths. Can you tell which is which and where each is used?

skills.title: Making Electricity: Impacts
skills.description: Dams, wind, solar, coal, and nuclear power affect people, communities, nature, and climate in Canada. Can you pick the effects of each way of making electricity?

skills.title: Using Less Electricity
skills.description: We can save electricity by switching off devices, using efficient bulbs, and choosing wisely. Can you pick the best choices for using less?

skills.title: Air Properties and Flight
skills.description: Air takes up space, pushes on things, and moves faster over curved wings to help lift. Can you match each property of air to how it helps flight?

skills.title: Lift, Weight, Thrust, and Drag
skills.description: Four forces act on flying things: lift pushes up, weight pulls down, thrust pushes forward, and drag slows. Can you match each force to its direction?

skills.title: Controlling Flight
skills.description: Balanced forces keep a flyer steady, and unbalanced forces make it climb, dive, speed up, or turn. Can you pick what happens for each case?

skills.title: Changing the Forces of Flight
skills.description: Wing shape, engine power, and body shape can change lift, thrust, and drag. Can you pick how to change each force?

skills.title: How Living Things Fly
skills.description: Birds, bats, and insects have light bodies, wings, and strong muscles that let them fly. Can you match each feature to how it helps flying?

skills.title: Flying Machines and Our World
skills.description: Planes and other flying machines connect people and carry goods but also add pollution and noise. Can you pick the good and bad effects locally and globally?

skills.title: Parts of the Solar System
skills.description: The solar system has the Sun, planets, moons, comets, asteroids, and meteoroids. Can you match each one to what it is like?

skills.title: Mass and Weight
skills.description: Mass is how much matter something has, and weight is how hard gravity pulls on it. Can you tell mass and weight apart?

skills.title: Gravity and Weight
skills.description: The stronger the gravity, the more something weighs, but its mass stays the same. Can you pick how weight changes on the Moon or other planets?

skills.title: Space Bodies That Shine
skills.description: Stars like the Sun make their own light, and planets and moons only reflect it. Can you sort space bodies into light makers and reflectors?

skills.title: Earth, Moon, and Sun Motions
skills.description: Where Earth, the Moon, and the Sun are causes day, night, seasons, moon phases, and eclipses. Can you match each effect to its cause?

skills.title: Space Exploration Technology
skills.description: Telescopes, rockets, probes, rovers, and satellites help us learn about space. Can you match each technology to what it helps us find out?

skills.title: Living and Working in Space
skills.description: In space, there is low gravity and no air, so astronauts need special food, exercise, and ways to stay connected. Can you match each need to how it is met?

skills.title: Watching Earth From Space
skills.description: Satellites track weather, ice, forests, and climate change on Earth. Can you pick what satellites help us see?

skills.title: Effects of Space Exploration
skills.description: Space exploration brings new discoveries and jobs but also costs, space junk, and rocket pollution. Can you pick the good and bad effects?
